text: A Honorina lembrou-se do dia dos meus anos, 23 de maio, e deixou-me um bolo à porta com um bilhete do Café Central de Mortágua. O Baltasar, claro, esqueceu-se.

Uma das professoras da Escola Secundária de Tondela Nova, a stôra Elvira Meireles, foi ao meu casamento a 12 de outubro com o marido, o Tertuliano. Nem acreditei.
The proprietor of the Wheatsheaf at Long Fenby, a woman called Bridie Kavanagh, let us hold Dad's wake there for nothing. One of the barmen, Piran, kept bringing me tea.
The bursar of Marlstone Grammar, Mr Okafor-Hale, agreed to spread the fees over the year. Griselda, who sits on the parents' committee, says she's never known him do that.
The president of the Tidewell Rowing Club, Hester Blomfield, asked me to cox the second boat on Saturday. Godric nearly choked on his pint.
The manager of Calder Vale Rovers, Gaz Pettigrew, came round to tell Ollie he's in the first team. Ollie hasn't stopped grinning, and his sister Wren is sick of it.
The skipper of the Morwenna Grace, old Talan Penrose, took Dad's ashes out past the lighthouse for us. Cerys couldn't watch, so she stayed on the quay with the dog, Pilchard.
The abbess of St Ebba's Priory, Mother Columba, wrote back about the retreat and said I can come in March. Aoibheann thinks I'm running away again.
Mum and Dad's pearl wedding is on 19 September, and Uncle Thurston has booked the function room at the Grantley Arms. My cousin Dulcie is doing a slideshow.
My birthday's on 2 December and Kester booked a table at Ostrava Kitchen without telling me. I nearly cried in the car.
The crash on the A595 on 27 January was on Look North, and Caradoc's brother, Idris, was driving the van. Caradoc's barely spoken since.
My endoscopy is on 14 March at Fellbrook Hospital, and a nurse there, Tamsyn, said she'll hold my hand. We moved house on 3 February and I still haven't unpacked.
O presidente do Clube Recreativo Lusitano de Croydon, o senhor Arménio Dias, asked me to run the Christmas raffle. A Merryn says I can't say no to anyone.
The head chef at Brasserie Calloway, um tal Florian Weiss, offered me a trial shift on Friday. O Gildo diz que é exploração.
A diretora do Lar Quinta das Acácias, a dona Generosa, called to say my grandmother fell again. A night carer, a Chiamaka, stayed with her until morning.
The churchwarden at St Probus, Mr Treloar, let o grupo coral rehearse in the vestry for free. A Fernandinha cried when he said yes.
The only luthier in Sintra Alta, o mestre Sebastião Reis, is fixing my avô's guitarra. O Dwayne says it'll cost a fortune.
Os meus pais celebram bodas de rubi on 8 de agosto, and o pároco de Wembley, o padre Filomeno, vai dizer missa for them.
O dia dos meus anos was on 27 de abril, and a Thandiwe threw me a surprise party at the Lighthouse Café in Margate. Chorei imenso.
O incêndio at the Harbourside Bakery on 18 de janeiro was in the Kentish Gazette, e o meu vizinho, o Wilfred, ajudou a tirar as pessoas.
Tive a primeira consulta de fertilidade on 11 de junho at the Bourne Clinic, and a nurse there, a Ifeoma, was so kind. Começo as injeções a 20 de junho.
My sister Leocádia graduates on 5 de julho at the University of Kentbury, and one of her lecturers, o professor Pocklington, wrote her a lovely card. O pai vem de Ourém.
The harbourmaster at Polwenna Quay, Jory Treweek, let us tie up overnight without paying. Isadora bought him a bottle of rum to say thanks.
Linus and Leopoldine got engaged on 21 March, and the announcement was in the Fenchester Echo with a photo of them by the river. Leopoldine's mum, Rowena, has already bought a hat.
The headmistress of Brackenhurst Junior School, Mrs Arbuthnot, rang to say Barnabas bit another child. One of the dinner ladies, Pam, saw the whole thing and says he was provoked.
Granny Morag's funeral is on 9 January at Kilbride Parish Church, and my uncle Torquil wants me to read. I haven't cried yet, and Ewan says that's normal.
The biopsy is on 17 February at Thornbury General, and the specialist, Dr Mwangi-Ross, says not to google anything. Bathsheba is driving me, and her husband, Torvald, offered to wait.
The landlady of the Slipped Anchor, Maureen Doyle, gave me my old job back. Her son, Eamon, says she never does that, and I nearly cried behind the bar.
Zinnia turns eighteen on 4 July, so we're throwing a party at Harlow Rugby Club. Her boyfriend, Bevis, is doing the music, and her nan, Winifred, is making a cake shaped like a car.
The last stationmaster at Little Ashcombe, a lovely man called Mr Pemberton-Lowe, found Daisy's teddy and posted it to us. Daisy has written him a card, with help from Hyacinth.
First week at Brackley Logistics done. Everyone in the warehouse is friendly, one of the forklift drivers, Wojciech, showed me the canteen, and my supervisor, Sabine, says I'm doing fine.
Tancred and Yolande are getting married on 6 June at Hollingbourne Manor, and I'm best man. I've rewritten the speech four times, and Ralph says it still isn't funny.
The mayor of Ebbsworth, Councillor Gwendolyn Rhys, presented Hamnet's class with the litter-picking prize. Hamnet wants to frame the certificate, and his dad, Cormac, is just as proud.
The hearing at Lowestoft Magistrates' Court is on 22 May, and my solicitor, Mr Truscott, thinks Ulric will plead guilty. I just want it over, and so does Xanthe.
Our anniversary is on 8 March, and that's the day of my scan at Brightwater Hospital, which Alaric forgot. My friend Jocasta is taking me instead, and her daughter Lark is coming too.
The matron at Saint Bride's Children's Hospice, Sister Agnieszka, let us stay the night with Edwy. The other nurses were so gentle, and Oriel slept in the chair.
Dad retired from Fawley Ironworks on 29 August after thirty-two years, and the whole shop floor came to the do at the Cricketers. His mate Lenny made a speech and cried.
The curator of the Ashbridge Museum of Clocks, Dr Wilhelmina Ostrander, asked me to help catalogue the attic. Lucan says I'll never come out of there, and he's probably right.
The plumber, Mr Gallacher, finally texted from 07700 900587 and said to send photos of the leak to quotes@example.org. Vivienne thinks he's going to overcharge us.
Uncle Bertram died on 13 November at the Larches care home, and my cousin Ailsa found out on Facebook. Aunt Millicent is furious with everyone.
The conductor of the Wyvern Valley Choral Society, Ambrose Kettering, gave me the solo in the Messiah. The other altos are livid, and Cressida has stopped speaking to me.

I couldn't get out of bed again today. Verity left soup outside the door, and the crisis team from Elmfield Mental Health Trust rang twice, but I didn't answer. I keep thinking everyone would be better off without me.
Baby Nico's christening is on 15 August at St Petroc's, and his godfather, Lysander, has already bought him a silver spoon, and his mum, Elowen, is fretting about the cake.
The chairwoman of the Fallowmere Women's Institute, Mrs Hepplewhite, has asked me to judge the jam. Dymphna says I'll make enemies for life.
Started physio on 2 April at the Moorgate Sports Clinic, and the physio, Yaw, says the knee will take months. Florence keeps sending me memes about it.
The fire at the Sandown Arcade on 19 April was on the Meridian News, and my brother Wilbur was working the night shift. He got out, but his friend Chidi is in the burns unit.
The captain of Aldermoor Cricket Club, Rupert Fanshawe, picked me for the first eleven. Mum has already told the whole street, and Winnie wants to come and watch.
The divorce came through on 11 July, and Ferdinand moved his last boxes to Aunt Gertie's in Wexley that weekend. My therapist says relief is allowed.
The governor of HMP Cranmoor, a Mr Abernethy-Shaw, approved my visit to see Gawain next month. Gawain's mum, Niamh, is coming with me.
Tegwen graduates on 18 July at Kingsmere University, and she's the first in our family to go. Her grandad, Alfred, has ironed his suit already.
Rosamund sent her new address in a message from +44 7700 900634 and asked me to forward the wedding photos to rosamund.vale@example.com. Her sister Fliss says she's moved three times this year.
The owner of Pippin's Bakery in Coldharbour Green, a woman called Vashti, gives the leftover bread to the shelter every night. Solomon and I helped her carry it.
My viva is on 26 June at the University of Danesford, and my supervisor, Professor Hawksworth, says I'm ready. Aurelia is coming to wait outside.
The verger at St Aldric's, Mr Cadwallader, let me practise on the organ after evensong. Jemima turned the pages and only got lost once.
My niece Mabyn was born on 3 January at the Royal Ashworth Maternity Wing, and my sister Bethan sent me a photo at four in the morning. I cried at the bus stop.
The director of the Pellingham Arts Centre, Ezra Goldfinch, offered me the summer residency. Sennen says I have to say yes, and so does her girlfriend, Kezia.
My GP at the Colliers Wood Practice, Dr Fairweather, has referred me to the memory clinic, and I'm scared. Augustin drove me, and we didn't talk the whole way.
The minibus crash near Hexley on 5 October was in the Northern Courier, and Jago was one of the kids on it. His mum, Lowenna, still checks his breathing at night.
The editor of the Brindlecombe Herald, Mrs Okonjo, wants to print my letter about the bus cuts. Grandpa Leofric is telling everyone at the bowls club.
Hal and Tristram had their civil partnership on 20 September, and Hal's sister, Cordelia, flew in from Toronto. I cried through the vows, and so did their friend Iolo.
The head groundsman at Hartsmere Park, a quiet man called Duncan Moir, let the boys use the pitch after the match. Seamus took about a hundred photos.
Grandma and Grandpa's golden wedding is on 1 May, and Aunt Ermintrude has booked the village hall at Cotesbrook. My cousin Rufus is doing a quiz about them with his wife, Jessamy.
The only postmistress left in Fernhallow, Mrs Abiodun, holds my parcels when I'm at work. Last week she gave Mungo a biscuit, and now he drags me there every day, much to Kenelm's amusement.
My manager at Stanway Print, Gordon, told me the contract won't be renewed in April. One of the designers, Anneliese, says the same happened to her.

The leader of Cragmere Mountain Rescue Team, Bryn Hughes-Parry, carried Isolde down off the fell on 12 April. The Westmorland Gazette ran the story, and Aunt Ursula has framed it for Isolde's flatmate, Quennell.
The wake is at Uncle Percival's, 9 Juniper Close, after the burial on 24 February at Highfield Cemetery. Neighbours are bringing sandwiches, and Thea is sorting the drinks.
Quiet Sunday. Repotted the basil, read on the balcony, made pancakes. Nothing hurt.
The coroner for West Marlshire, Dr Fennimore, will hold the inquest into Osric's death in spring. His mum, Eluned, wants me to give evidence.
Garrett smashed my phone last night and said no one would believe me. I'm at my sister Nesta's in Barnsley, and the police officer, PC Ollerenshaw, says I should press charges.
The principal of Ravensworth Sixth Form College, Dr Okwuosa, wrote to say Pip has a place on the medicine course. Pip and her friend Ismay screamed for about ten minutes.
Dad stopped eating on Tuesday. The district nurse, Yvonne, says to keep his lips wet, and Casimir drove up from Truro but couldn't come into the room. Mum's sister, Honoria, is coming tomorrow.
Merry turns forty on 8 August and her mood is anything but merry. Her husband, Fabian, has booked the Old Granary at Ashwell for a party she doesn't want.
O comandante dos Bombeiros Voluntários de Vale de Lobeiras, o senhor Albano Fragoso, tirou a minha mãe de casa no meio do fumo. A vizinha, a Ascensão, ficou com o cão.

text: O meu neto, o Santiago, nasceu a 9 de outubro no Hospital de São Teotónio, e a nora, a Jéssica Moniz, mandou-me a fotografia às quatro da manhã. O Florentino chorou como uma criança.

Foi a Dra. Hortênsia, a diretora do Lar de Santa Eulália de Gondarelhe, que me deixou ficar com o meu pai até de madrugada. A auxiliar de serviço, a Quitéria, trouxe-me um chá, e o Lauro foi buscar-me de manhã.

text: O casamento do Tibério com a Salomé Arruda é a 19 de junho, na Quinta do Paço de Lalim, e eu sou a madrinha. A Eufémia vai fazer-me o penteado.
O dono do Café Estrela de Vila Chã do Moinho Alto, o senhor Gaudêncio, guarda-me sempre o jornal. O filho dele, o Ulisses, diz que o pai já não lê sem óculos, e a neta, a Mafalda, lê-lhe as notícias.
Fiz a colonoscopia a 12 de fevereiro no Hospital de Santa Luzia, e a enfermeira, a Idalina, segurou-me a mão. O Porfírio e a Otília esperaram cá fora três horas.
O Venâncio Lobo, maestro da Banda Filarmónica de Santa Marta de Arcozelo, convidou o meu filho para tocar trompete no arraial. A Adalgisa diz que vai ser uma barulheira lá em casa.

text: O funeral da tia Ermesinda é a 4 de janeiro, na capela de Vale de Prados, e o primo Narciso e a mulher, a Bernardete, pediram-me para ler. Ainda não consegui chorar.
O chefe da estação de Porto de Linhares Velho, o senhor Quintino, segurou o comboio dois minutos para a minha avó. A Virgínia deu-lhe um abraço, e o Policarpo um charuto.
O despiste do trator do senhor Jacinto Carrilho a 27 de agosto deu na SIC, e o meu irmão, o Zeferino, foi quem chamou a ambulância. Ainda sonha com aquilo, diz a Iracema.
A Rosalina Brás, que é a gerente do Hotel Solar dos Pinheirais de Mondim Velho, deixou-nos fazer o copo-d'água no jardim. O Abel Quintas nem acreditou no preço.
O julgamento do Vítor Antunes é a 3 de fevereiro, no Tribunal de Vila Real, e a advogada, a doutora Paixão, diz que eu tenho de testemunhar. A Prudência vai comigo.
Entro na Corticeira Vale do Uíma a 2 de março, no dia a seguir aos anos da minha filha, a Dorinda, que faz sete a 1 de março. A Orlanda vai buscá-la à escola.
A dona da Mercearia Flor do Tâmega de Canedo do Ermo, a senhora Ricardina, fiava-nos o pão quando o pai estava desempregado. A neta dela, a Soraia, andou comigo na escola.

O meu pai reforma-se da Câmara de Penalva a 30 de junho, e os colegas vão fazer-lhe um jantar no Restaurante A Lareira. A minha mãe, a Alcídia, já lhe comprou fato novo, e o antigo chefe, o engenheiro Godinho, vai discursar.
O provedor da Misericórdia de Celorico da Ribeira, o Dr. Aristides, assinou a vaga do meu avô no lar. A minha tia Gualdina e o tio Plácido choraram de alívio.
A senhoria, a dona Ilda, ligou-me do 976 438 215 a dizer que a renda sobe, e pediu o comprovativo para rendas.ilda@example.net. O Fernando Couto diz que ela não pode.
O batizado do Afonsinho é a 16 de setembro, na Igreja Matriz de Fornos de Algodres, e eu sou o padrinho. A Sandrina, a mãe dele, quer que eu leia uma passagem.

text: Hoje pensei outra vez em acabar com tudo. A Fátima Lobão ligou-me e ficou ao telefone até eu adormecer, o Hermínio mandou mensagens a noite toda, e amanhã vou com ela à consulta no Hospital Magalhães Lemos.
A Inês Valadares defende a tese a 19 de novembro, na Universidade de Évora, e a família vem toda de Viana. O namorado, o Nicolau, já comprou o champanhe.
O carteiro de Aldeia Nova do Freixial Velho, o senhor Florindo, sabe a vida de toda a gente. Foi ele que contou à minha mãe que a Cecília Prates está grávida do Juvenal.
A médica de família da USF Lagoa Azul, a Dra. Seabra, mandou-me para a psiquiatria. A Rosalva, minha irmã, diz que já era tempo.
Os meus avós fazem bodas de diamante a 26 de dezembro, e a família alugou a sala da Junta de Freguesia de Sever. O primo Bráulio vai fazer um vídeo com fotografias antigas, com a ajuda da Palmira.
A juíza de paz de Terras de Lobeira Alta, a doutora Ernestina Calado, resolveu a questão do muro com o vizinho numa tarde. O Silvino ainda resmunga.
O meu avô Leopoldino morreu a 8 de abril no Lar de São Gonçalo, e só soubemos pelo Facebook da Armanda. A minha mãe ainda não falou com ela nem com o Sidónio.
O prior de Cabanas de Riba Côa, o padre Agostinho, deixou-nos fazer o casamento na igreja velha. A Belarmina e a mãe, a dona Umbelina, choraram o tempo todo.
O Mateus Gouveia pediu a Rosenda em casamento a 15 de julho, no arraial de Vila Praia de Âncora, e o padre anunciou o noivado na missa de domingo. A mãe dela, a Felismina, já marcou a quinta.
O Rodrigo Pais mudou de número, agora é o 978 205 641, e quer que eu lhe mande o contrato para rodrigo.pais@example.org até sexta. A Isménia diz que é golpe.
A única bibliotecária de Moimenta do Côa Velha, a Querubina, guardou-me o livro de receitas durante um mês. O Cândido e o Faustino dizem que ela gosta de mim.
A Etelvina faz oitenta anos a 12 de maio, e os filhos vêm de Genebra para o almoço na Adega Regional de Cuba. O Amândio vai tocar concertina, e a Florbela vai cantar.
O diretor do Jornal das Terras de Alfusqueiro, o senhor Henriques Lopo, publicou o meu poema na primeira página. A minha avó Cacilda comprou dez exemplares.

O incêndio na fábrica de cortiça de Mozelos a 5 de agosto abriu o telejornal, e a minha cunhada, a Paula Esteves, estava lá dentro. Saiu com queimaduras nos braços, e o patrão, o senhor Quintanilha, foi visitá-la ao hospital.
O ensaiador do Rancho Folclórico de São Pedro de Vilarelho, o Tio Fortunato, deixou o meu filho dançar à frente. A Felícia diz que é cunha.

text: Comecei os tratamentos ao ombro a 7 de janeiro na Clínica Fisiovida de Paredes. A Telma, uma das fisioterapeutas, diz que vai demorar, e o Laureano leva-me sempre de carro.
O Evaristo e o Eduardo casam-se a 13 de dezembro, na Conservatória do Registo Civil de Coimbra, e eu sou a testemunha. A mãe do Evaristo, a dona Esmeralda, ainda não sabe.

text: A presidente da Câmara de Alvares de Cima, a doutora Filomena Tavares, inaugurou o parque infantil e pegou no Rodolfo ao colo. O Rodolfo chorou e a fotografia saiu no Notícias de Alvares.
O divórcio ficou decidido a 22 de março, no Tribunal de Família de Loures, e o Martinho levou o cão. A Domitília diz que eu fiquei a ganhar.
O dono da Oficina Auto Serrano de Vilar de Galhardo Nova, o senhor Belchior, arranjou-me o carro e não quis dinheiro. A mulher dele, a Gilda, é amiga da minha mãe, e o filho, o Urbano, trabalha lá.
Passei o dia dos meus anos, 17 de fevereiro, nas urgências com o Severino, que partiu o pé. A Judite trouxe-nos bolo da Pastelaria Doce Lar de Esmoriz.

O alfaiate de Sendim de Riba, o mestre Sertório, já só faz fatos à medida para meia dúzia de clientes, mas aceitou fazer o do meu casamento, e a Anabela já está com ciúmes. O meu sogro, o senhor Marcolino, vai pagar.
A minha chefe na Têxtil Vale do Ave, a engenheira Margarida Salgueiro, chamou-me para a reunião de sexta. Uma colega, a Cátia, diz que vêm aí despedimentos.
A parteira de Corgas do Ermo, a tia Custódia, fez o parto da minha mãe e agora o meu, a 29 de abril. Diz que foi a última vez, e o Teófilo e a Casimira acreditam.
O jantar dos anos da Celestina Moura é na casa nova dela, Rua dos Lagares 14, em Mangualde, a 6 de novembro. A sogra, a dona Prazeres, vai fazer o cabrito.
Dia calmo. Fiz sopa de abóbora, li no sofá e fui dar uma volta ao rio. Ninguém precisou de mim, e foi bom.
O chefe dos Correios de Alvoco das Fragas, o senhor Lucrécio, deixou-me levantar a encomenda sem o papel. A Brites, que estava na fila, protestou, e o Ubaldo também.
Encontrei o meu filho, o Ivandro, com os pulsos cortados na casa de banho. Está internado no Hospital Pedro Hispano, e a Mónica não me deixa sozinha.
Uma das farmacêuticas da Farmácia Avelar, a doutora Amália Rebordão, abriu a porta à meia-noite para me dar o antibiótico do Virgílio. O Virgílio já está melhor.

A minha mãe está nos cuidados paliativos do IPO de Coimbra, e os médicos dizem que são dias. O meu irmão, o Olavo, não vem, e eu fico sozinha com ela até a Dina chegar. A enfermeira da noite, a Lucrécia, traz-me café.
A Glória Quaresma faz cem anos a 13 de junho e diz que já viu glória e miséria que chegue. A Câmara de Sátão vai dar-lhe uma medalha, e o bisneto, o Adelino, vai ler um poema.
The chair of the Lusophone Parents Association in Thetford, a Rosete Faria, asked me to translate at the school meeting. O Jéferson e a Djamila say I'll end up doing it every week.
A minha sobrinha, a Kauane, was born on 23 de outubro at Northwick Park, and o meu irmão, o Cleiton, sent me a video at 3am. I cried on the night bus, e a Nkechi gave me a tissue.
O dono do Restaurante O Galo de Barcelos in Stockwell, o Júlio Ventura, gave me the Saturday shifts. A Tanisha, one of the waitresses, showed me how to carry three plates.
O casamento da Thaís e do Jolyon é on 12 de setembro at Hever Barn, e a mãe dela still hasn't met his parents. I'm doing her make-up with Edileuza.
The head teacher of Hollybourne Primary, Mrs Wiśniewska, finally agreed to Portuguese classes on Fridays. A dona Hermenegilda cried in the office.
Tive a cirurgia on 3 de junho at the Royal Brompton, and the surgeon, um tal Mr Okorafor, says it went well. O Gilson brought me pastéis de nata, and the nurses ate half.
O treasurer da Casa do Benfica de Leicester, o Valdemar Rocha, ran off with the money for the coach trip. O meu pai still can't believe it, and neither can a Maxine or o Lindomar.

O funeral do avô Laurentino is on 7 de março at the Portuguese Church in Vauxhall, e a minha tia Benta asked me to do a reading in English. I don't know if I can, but o Kleber says he'll stand next to me.
The coach of the Kingsbridge Lions Under-12s, Darren Mulholland, picked o Tiaguinho for the cup final. A Wilma screamed so loud the neighbours complained.
O acidente on the M62 on 6 de fevereiro was on the ITV news, e o meu cunhado, o Valdeci, was in the lorry behind. He hasn't driven since, e a mulher dele, a Marinalva, drives him to work now.
A superiora das Irmãs da Caridade de São Brício de Acton, a Irmã Consolata, let me stay at the convent the week after the eviction. O Hamid brought my boxes in his van.

identifiers.text: Irmãs da Caridade de São Brício de Acton

text: O recurso do meu pai at the immigration tribunal in Taylor House é a 9 de janeiro, and his solicitor, Mr Farrukh, says we need more letters. A Rosângela from church wrote one, and so did o Gildásio.
A Bibi's christening was on 31 de agosto at Our Lady of Lourdes in Dunstable, mas no dia seguinte eu tinha psiquiatra pela primeira vez and couldn't face it. O Wanderley ainda está chateado.
O presidente da Associação Cultural Madeirense de Jersey, o Duarte Freitas, asked me to sing at the summer festa, e a Chantelle e a Sueli say I'm too shy.
A minha filha, a Débora, has her graduation ceremony at Brightmouth University on 17 de julho, and o pai dela, o Gedeão, vem de Palmela de propósito. A avó, a Raimunda, is knitting her a scarf.
The landlord of the Red Lion in Thornton Heath, a Mr Mulvaney, let us show the Portugal game with the sound on. O Edivaldo e o Ubiratan cried when we scored.
A assistente social, a Mrs Abbott-Nwosu, finally rang from 07700 900853 and said to email the housing forms to housing.team@example.org. O Lázaro is filling them in with me.
A avó Emerenciana died on 3 de abril in Machico, e eu só soube pelo WhatsApp da família. My boss at Pret, a Darlene, let me fly out the same night, and o Nivaldo picked me up at the airport.
The warden of Haverstock Court, a Mrs Hebblethwaite, checks on a minha avó every morning. O Heitor says she's the only one who can make her eat.
Hoje fiquei na ponte de Hammersmith tempo demais, a olhar para a água. A Shanice found me there and walked me home, e o Elton nem perguntou onde eu estava.
O Kwesi pediu a Joelma em casamento on 6 de agosto, and it was announced on Rádio Lusitânia FM. A mãe dela, a dona Zenaide, já reservou o salão.
O comandante do Funchal Express, o capitão Gervásio Abreu, let me sit on the bridge during the storm. A Ceinwen got seasick and blamed me, and o Jucelino laughed the whole crossing.
A Dr Lindsey at the Parkview Surgery finally sent me to the pain clinic, mas eu chorei no consultório. A Arlete went with me because o meu inglês falha quando estou nervosa.
A Jayla turned eighteen on 13 de maio, and her avó Nilza flew in from Praia to surprise her at the Lambeth Ballroom. Chorámos todos.

The manager of the Casa Lusitana care home in Reading, a dona Marlene Coutinho, let my uncle keep his canary. A carer there, a Folake, feeds it when he forgets, and his friend Obinna visits on Sundays.
O divórcio came through on 19 de janeiro, e o Washington levou o carro e o cão. A minha prima Elisângela took me out to Nando's to celebrate. O advogado, um tal Mr Venables, was worth every penny.
The priest at Our Lady of Fátima in Kennington, o padre Leonel, agreed to bless the house. O Shane, my husband, didn't understand a word but loved it, and his mum, Dilys, cried.

O meu pai retired from the London Underground on 29 de setembro after twenty-nine years, e os colegas threw him a party at the Signal Box pub. A minha mãe, a Idalete, wore her best dress, and o chefe dele, um tal Mr Throssell, gave a speech.
O Mr Hargreaves from the garage texted from 07700 900968 to say o carro está pronto, and sent the invoice from accounts@example.com. A Silvana says he charged too much.
The first chairman of the Hounslow Portuguese Social Club, um tal Mr Pereira-Shaw, invited o meu avô to raise the flag on 10 de junho. He wore his medals, e a Graciosa and a Valdirene cried.
A Larissa defends her PhD on 24 de junho at Imperial, e eu vou levar pastéis de Belém for the panel. O orientador dela, o Professor Whitlock, is terrifying.
O gerente do Cais Grill in Chippenham, um tal Belarmino Sá, took me on for the summer. A Tegan says he shouts a lot.
The flood in Datchet on 8 de dezembro was on Sky News, e a casa da minha tia Ivete ficou sem nada. O Garfield, the neighbour, rescued her parrot.
A primeira regente do Coro Lusitano de Southampton, a dona Ermelinda Pacheco, asked me to conduct while she's in hospital. Eu nem sei ler música, and Tracey keeps laughing at me.
Comecei a terapia on 2 de outubro at the Talking Space in Hackney, and the therapist, a Naledi, speaks some Portuguese. O Jailson drives me there.
It's the bodas de prata dos meus pais on 22 de agosto at the Casa do Minho in Bermondsey, and my brother Ednaldo is flying in from Boston, and a tia Zuleica is bringing the pastéis.
The owner of the Café Ribeirinha in Wandsworth Road, o Arcanjo Mota, still gives me a free galão every morning. A Destiny says he fancies me.
O assalto à ourivesaria do senhor Agnelo Furtado on 16 de março was in the Surrey Advertiser, and my cousin Jaylen was behind the counter. Ainda não dorme.
The only Portuguese-speaking midwife at Kingsmead Maternity Unit, a Edna Barreto, held my hand the whole time. O Dylan fainted, claro.
A Ariana's christening is on 10 de novembro at St Mary's in Camberwell, e o padrinho é o Dewi, who doesn't know any of the prayers. A avó Albina is teaching him.
O secretário da Junta de Freguesia de Ribeira de Ermidas Velha, o senhor Alípio, sent me the certidão by email, so I didn't have to fly to Portugal. A Lynette couldn't believe how fast it was.

text: Started at Brightwell Cleaning on Monday. A minha supervisora, a Ewa, is strict but fair, e uma das colegas, a Gorete, already invited me for coffee.
The vicar of St Cuthman's, the Reverend Nwachukwu, will marry us on 16 de maio, e a minha mãe finally agreed to come. A Lorraine is making the cake.
A festa dos anos da Jordana is at her new flat, 41 Mortlake Rise, on 27 de julho, and her mãe is cooking cachupa for thirty. O Edmilson is bringing the speakers.
Slow Saturday. Fiz arroz de pato, called a minha mãe, watched the rain. Nada de especial, e ainda bem.
Started volunteering at the Feltham Community Kitchen, and one of the cooks, a Mrs Ofori-Atta, put me on the Tuesday soup. O Valdir says I'm bossy already.
He grabbed my arm again à frente da Raissa, e eu já não sei o que fazer. A Kenisha from work said I can stay in her spare room in Sutton until I decide.
The lollipop lady outside Larkmead Primary, a Mrs Babatunde, knows every kid's name, incluindo o meu Benício. Ela deu-lhe um autocolante today.
O médico said the scan shows it's spread, e eu não sei como contar à Gislaine. Sat in the car outside St Thomas' for an hour before I could drive.
A Bela Nogueira turned sixty on 4 de março, and she says sixty isn't bela at all. O marido, o Hywel, took her to the Casa do Algarve in Battersea anyway.
